clusters.name: Core Diagnostic Criteria (DSM-5-TR)
items: Criterion A: Restriction of energy intake relative to requirements leading to significantly low body weight (BMI-for-age <5th percentile or fallen off growth curve) (DSM p.381, Dulcan p.412)
Criterion B: Intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, or persistent behavior interfering with weight gain (DSM p.381, Dulcan p.412)
Criterion C: Disturbance in body weight/shape perception, undue influence on self-evaluation, or lack of recognition of seriousness of low weight (DSM p.381, Dulcan p.412)

criteria.thresholds: All 3 criteria (A, B, C) required; severity based on BMI or BMI percentile (DSM p.381)
subtypes: Restricting type (F50.01): No binge/purge in last 3 months; weight loss via dieting, fasting, excessive exercise (DSM p.381, Dulcan p.412)
Binge-eating/purging type (F50.02): Recurrent binge eating or purging (self-induced vomiting, laxatives, diuretics, enemas) in last 3 months (DSM p.381, Dulcan p.412)

epidemiology.prevalence: Lifetime prevalence ~0.6%-0.8% in adults (0.9%-1.42% females, 0.12%-0.3% males); 0.3% full / 0.8% subthreshold in adolescents (DSM p.384, Dulcan p.417)
epidemiology.sex_ratio: ~10:1 F:M in adults (12-month 0.4%-0.9% F vs 0.03% M); narrower gap in adolescents (DSM p.384)
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: 12-18 years (mid-to-late adolescence); peak onset during adolescence (DSM p.385, Dulcan p.411)
epidemiology.heritability: 22%-76% for AN and subthreshold AN (Dulcan p.416)
comorbidities: Anxiety disorders (GAD, Social Anxiety, OCD) (DSM p.387, Dulcan p.417)
Major Depressive Disorder / Bipolar Disorder (DSM p.387, Dulcan p.417)
Substance Use Disorders (more common in binge/purge type) (DSM p.384, Dulcan p.417)
epidemiology.prognosis: ~75% full recovery in adolescents (median 5 years); ~50% full recovery in adults, 30% partial, 20% chronic (Dulcan p.421)

etiology.genetic: Heritability 22%-76%; GWAS identified risk loci shared with OCD, MDD, Tourette's and metabolic traits (insulin/lipids) (DSM p.385, Dulcan p.416, 437)
etiology.neurobiology: Shift from ventral striatum (reward) to dorsal striatum/OFC (habit/compulsion); 5-HT2C receptor dysregulation (satiety/obsessions); altered DA reward processing in ventral striatum (DSM p.385, StahlNeuro p.125, 184, 538-541)
etiology.environmental: Sociocultural thin-ideal internalization, high-risk occupations (ballet, modeling, athletics), controlling/enmeshed family environment (DSM p.384-385, Dulcan p.416, 418)

first_line: Family-Based Treatment (FBT / Maudsley) — Gold standard 3-phase outpatient psychotherapy for children and adolescents (Dulcan p.425-426)
Inpatient medical admission for acute refeeding and hemodynamic stabilization (Dulcan p.421, 613)
second_line: Adolescent-Focused Individual Therapy (AFT) or CBT-E if FBT unavailable/failed (Dulcan p.426-429)
Olanzapine (Off-label) for severe obsessionality, severe anxiety around meals, and weight gain (Dulcan p.429, StahlKids p.351, 356)
key_side_effects: Olanzapine: significant weight gain, sedation, metabolic dysregulation (hyperglycemia, dyslipidemia), neutropenia (StahlKids p.351, 354, 356)
Fluoxetine/SSRIs: ineffective for weight gain in acute starvation/underweight (Dulcan p.429)
treatment.monitoring: Olanzapine: Baseline & monthly weight/BMI z-score for 3 months then quarterly; baseline, 3-month, annual fasting glucose/lipids & BP; CBC for ANC <1000/mm3 (StahlKids p.351, Dulcan p.827)

items: Eating Disorder Examination (EDE) & Child EDE (ChEDE) — semi-structured gold standard diagnostic interviews (Dulcan p.424)
Parent EDE-Questionnaire (PEDE-Q) — parent-report measure of eating pathology (Dulcan p.424)
Eating Disorder Screen for Primary Care (ESP) — 5-item quick screening tool (Dulcan p.612)
CDC BMI-for-age growth charts — tracking <5th percentile or trajectory deflection (DSM p.382, Dulcan p.416, 612)
key_numbers: 5 screening questions in the ESP tool (Dulcan p.612)
<5th BMI-for-age percentile benchmark for underweight in youth (DSM p.382, Dulcan p.416)
<17.0 kg/m2 BMI threshold for significantly low weight in adults (DSM p.382)

items: Gastrointestinal: Celiac disease, Inflammatory Bowel Disease (Crohn's/UC), SMA syndrome, Achalasia (DSM p.386, Dulcan p.312, 423, 613)
Endocrine: Hyperthyroidism, Addison's disease, Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (diabulimia) (DSM p.384, 386, Dulcan p.325, 423)
Psychiatric: ARFID (lacks fat phobia/body image disturbance), MDD, OCD, Social Anxiety, BDD, PANS (DSM p.379, 383, 386-387, Dulcan p.371, 415)
key_numbers: 3 months duration requirement for AN subtypes vs acute PANS onset (DSM p.381, Dulcan p.371)
100% absence of body image disturbance required to diagnose ARFID over AN (DSM p.379, 387, Dulcan p.415)

items: Carbohydrate reintroduction triggers insulin surge driving phosphorus, potassium, and magnesium into cells (DSM p.385, Dulcan p.421, 613)
Severe hypophosphatemia causes ATP depletion, acute heart failure, respiratory muscle failure, rhabdomyolysis, and death (DSM p.385, Dulcan p.613)
Thiamine (Vitamin B1) supplementation required prior to carbohydrate refeeding to prevent Wernicke encephalopathy (Dulcan p.425)
key_numbers: 3 critical electrolytes shifted intracellularly: Phosphorus, Potassium, Magnesium (DSM p.385, Dulcan p.613)
1 daily electrolyte lab panel monitoring requirement during initial refeeding phase (Dulcan p.423)

items: Cardiovascular: Sinus bradycardia (<50 bpm), hypotension, QTc prolongation, mitral valve prolapse (MVP), cardiac atrophy (DSM p.385-386, Dulcan p.420, 613)
Endocrine/Bone: HPG axis suppression (amenorrhea/delayed menarche), Peak Bone Mass reduction (irreversible osteopenia/osteoporosis) (DSM p.383, 385, Dulcan p.420, Syllabus p.38)
Hematologic/GI: Bone marrow gelatinous transformation (leukopenia/neutropenia), gastroparesis, SMA syndrome, parotid hypertrophy, Russell's sign (DSM p.385-386, Dulcan p.420, 613)
key_numbers: 1 irreversible skeletal complication: Peak bone mass loss during adolescent window (DSM p.383, Dulcan p.420, Syllabus p.38)
<50 bpm resting heart rate threshold defining sinus bradycardia (Dulcan p.613)
>500 ms QTc interval threshold for severe arrhythmia risk (Dulcan p.832)

items: Phase 1: Parents take 100% control of refeeding and weight restoration; includes in-clinic Family Meal (Dulcan p.426)
Phase 2: Gradual handoff of eating control back to adolescent once weight reaches 87%-90% expected and compliance achieved (Dulcan p.426)
Phase 3: Focus shifts to normative adolescent development, autonomy, and healthy family relationships once weight is stable (Dulcan p.426)
Core stance: Agnostic regarding cause, externalization of illness from patient, parental empowerment (Dulcan p.425)
key_numbers: 3 distinct treatment phases in FBT-AN (Dulcan p.426)
70% full remission rate achieved at end of treatment and maintained at 5-year follow-up (Dulcan p.425-426)
87%-90% expected body weight threshold required before transitioning from Phase 1 to Phase 2 (Dulcan p.426)

high_yield: Anorexia nervosa has the highest crude mortality rate (~5% per decade) of any psychiatric disorder, primarily from cardiac collapse and suicide (DSM p.384, Dulcan p.421)
Suicide is the 2nd leading cause of death in AN, with an 18-fold increased risk compared to age/sex matched controls (DSM p.386)
Peak bone mass reduction during adolescence is an irreversible complication that does not fully recover even after weight restoration (DSM p.383, Dulcan p.420, Syllabus p.38)
Refeeding syndrome hallmark is severe hypophosphatemia triggered by carbohydrate-induced insulin release pushing phosphate into cells (DSM p.385, Dulcan p.613)
Family-Based Treatment (FBT / Maudsley) is the 1st-line gold standard treatment for adolescent AN, outperforming individual therapies in RCTs (Dulcan p.425-426)
SSRIs like fluoxetine are ineffective for weight gain or AN symptoms during acute starvation/underweight state (Dulcan p.429)
Olanzapine is the 1st-line off-label psychotropic for severe AN, targeting meal-related anxiety, obsessive food thoughts, and weight restoration (Dulcan p.429, StahlKids p.351, 356)
ARFID is distinguished from AN by the complete absence of fat phobia, fear of weight gain, or body image disturbance (DSM p.379, 387, Dulcan p.415)
Purging via self-induced vomiting causes metabolic alkalosis (hypokalemia, hypochloremia), whereas laxative abuse causes metabolic acidosis (DSM p.385)
Superior Mesenteric Artery (SMA) syndrome causes acute duodenal obstruction due to severe loss of the mesenteric fat pad (Dulcan p.613)
